title: Where Does 'I Don't Know' Live? Layerwise Onset of Refusal vs Abstention

original_idea.body:
# Where Does 'I Don't Know' Live? Layerwise Onset of Refusal vs Abstention

**Problem:** Whether harmful-refusal and epistemic-abstention share the same direction and emerge at the same layer has not been varied within one study.

**Direction:** Build two contrastive datasets (refusal; abstention). Extract a difference-of-means direction for each at every layer. Measure cross-direction cosine similarity per layer and test cross-steering.

**Why it matters:** Conflating safety refusal with honest uncertainty is a real alignment hazard: over-broad refusal directions can suppress legitimate hedging.

**Relevant context:** Arditi et al. 2024; representation-engineering truthfulness directions.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: disentangling safety-refusal from honest abstention addresses a concrete alignment hazard (over-refusal vs honesty leakage).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Two contrastive datasets + difference-of-means at each layer; guided, mentor helpful for dataset design.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: per-layer cosine similarity + cross-steering test, clear deliverable.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Honesty/refusal disentanglement labs deprioritize; public models, independent-friendly.

novelty.reasoning: Disentangling refusal vs abstention directions layerwise appears not directly studied.
